briefFidelity: FAIL. The brief asks for BARROW: one massive form that commands and overflows the frame, built from a few large members, charcoal and iron with a SINGLE ochre seam, fracturing under drawdown. Before reading it I described centred rotational emblems -- rosettes, starbursts, discs and scatter fields -- floating inside generous margin under 3-, 6- and 12-fold symmetry. Four separate mismatches, each independently disqualifying. (1) SCALE AND MASS: nothing is 'considerably larger than the frame comfortably holds'. Every token sits inside a clear black margin; the largest (9369, 9906, 10085) are discs that fill the middle and stop short of every edge. The only things touching an edge are stray small squares and triangles in 9548 and 10980 -- debris, not mass. (2) MEMBER COUNT: the brief says a few large members, explicitly not many small ones. 9011, 9548, 9727 and 10980 are built from a dozen-plus small scattered primitives; 9190 is a starburst of roughly twenty small triangles. That is the construction the brief rules out by name. (3) PALETTE: 'a single ochre seam' became a co-dominant hue. On 9369, 9906 and 10085 the ochre IS the entire mass -- a solid amber disc -- and on 9190 and 10443 it is the whole central figure. A seam is an accent inside a charcoal body; this inverts the ratio. (4) The construction language is radial/heraldic -- a badge, a rosette, a mandala -- and it reads decorative and weightless where the brief asks for brutalist, solemn and immovable. Weight is not the subject here; symmetry is.
seedVariation: PASS on this axis, and it is the one axis that is genuinely healthy. At 120px the twelve are not one work twelve times: solid disc (9369, 9906, 10085), dense starburst (9190), diamond (10443), large triangle outline (10264), tight cluster (9727), loose scatter (9548, 10980) are all distinct governing forms with different fold counts and different central scales. If anything the spread is wider than a single-monument family would want -- a solid amber disc and a field of drifting grey squares do not read as two conditions of the same kind of object -- but the failure here is under-cohesion, not sameness, and it is not the reason for the refusal.
thumbnailSurvival: PARTIAL FAIL. Eight of twelve read cleanly at 120px and stay separable by silhouette. Four do not: 9011, 10622, 10801 and 10980 are low-luminance slate-grey triangles on near-black and drop to near-invisible smudges -- at browse size the grid reads as roughly eight images and four blank tiles. This matters more than usual because the brief's stated reason for wanting a few large members is precisely that it 'reads as one silhouette' at browse size; the tokens that most violate the member-count rule are the same ones that vanish. Interior detail is also lost everywhere -- 9369's inner 12-point star collapses to a scalloped edge -- which is acceptable, but the grey-only tokens losing the whole image is not.
marketResponse: FAIL, and this is the clearest single defect. The change IS visible at browse size -- so it is not a dead transformation -- but it is not the claimed change and in places it is the inverse of it. The brief asks the mass to FRACTURE under drawdown: members separating, silhouette breaking. What actually happens between neutral and stress is that the ochre brightens and saturates, the central figure grows, and a new bright stroked outline is added on top: an amber triangle outline on 9011, an amber 12-point star outline on 9548, a larger and more saturated star on 9190, a larger disc on 9369. Nothing separates. No silhouette breaks. On 9190 and 9369 the mass gets bigger and more solid under stress -- consolidating exactly when it was supposed to be coming apart. Recovery does return close to neutral, so the three-state shape exists; it is just carrying the wrong content. The tokens whose neutral is already a scatter (9548, 10980) are dispersed in ALL three states, so their dispersion cannot be read as fracture either -- it is a constant, not a response.
tokenIdentity: PASS. This is the other axis that holds. Across all three rows each token stays unmistakably the same object: 9011 keeps its triangle arrangement, 9190 its six-point star and radiating triangles, 9369 its disc-with-dark-core, 9548 its square field with amber corners. Position, fold count and primitive are stable; only brightness, scale and the added outline move. One monument under three conditions is satisfied -- there is simply no fracture in it.
composition: Focal hierarchy is present and clean in the disc and star tokens (bright centre, dark core, quiet ground) and absent in the scatter tokens, where a dozen equal-weight small shapes give the eye nothing to land on. Frame use is the central problem: everything floats in a comfortable centred margin, which is the opposite of a form that overflows its frame, and the only edge contact is incidental clipping of small outlying members in 9548 and 10980 -- clipping that reads as an accident of scatter rather than as mass exceeding the frame. Overlap handling is decent at 256 (translucent slate triangles pool into readable darker plates) but mushes at 120, where the layered greys smear into one indistinct patch. No rendering artifacts, no banding, no stray geometry.
reasoning: I wrote my description before seeing the brief, and the gap between the two is not a matter of degree. I described centred, symmetrical, decorative emblems in ochre and slate on near-black -- rosettes and starbursts built from many small repeated primitives, floating inside generous margin, whose response to stress is to brighten, enlarge and gain an extra outline. The brief asks for a single brutalist mass too large for its frame, built from a few large members, charcoal-and-iron with one ochre seam, that comes apart under drawdown. The palette family and the three-state discipline are the only things that survive the comparison. Seed variation is healthy and token identity across conditions is solid, so this is competent work -- but competence is not the gate. It fails brief fidelity on scale, on member count, on the ochre ratio and on the form language, and it fails the named transformation outright: the mass does not fracture under stress, it consolidates and brightens. A claimed transformation that is visible but is the opposite of what was claimed is worse than one that is merely subtle, and this is a permanent on-chain commitment. REFUSE.
wouldChange: Build the actual subject first: ONE massive form, assembled from three to six large members, sized to exceed the frame so it is cropped by the edges rather than floating inside them, charcoal and iron with the ochre reduced to a single seam along one joint. Everything else follows from that -- once there is a mass made of large members, drawdown can do the thing the brief actually asks for, which is to separate those members and break the silhouette, instead of the current brighten-and-grow. Do not try to retrofit fracture onto the present radial rosettes; there are no members in them to separate.
